summary: Chadwick worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Cambridge and Clare College, also studying under Wilhelm Streitberg. At Cambridge, he was Elrington and Bosworth Professor of Anglo-Saxon (1910–1941) and held fellowships at Clare.

Schöhl was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the universities of Strasbourg, Freiburg, Munich, and Göttingen, and earned his PhD at Münster under Richard Schmidt (~1912–1914). He also studied under Ernst Leumann.
Aiyangar worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts in the Kannada (attested 1938) and Canarese (attested 1957) departments at the University of Madras.
Rao is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
Sunim specializes in Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Hu-von Hinüber is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. She earned an MA at Peking University under Kemo Jin and studied under Zhongxin Jiang. In 2010, she was a director at the University of Freiburg.

Kitamura was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), became president of Reitaku University (1986), and directed the Toyo Bunko (1990–2001).

Nakamura was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui and served there as professor (1954–1973), later directing the Eastern Institute (1973–1999).

Okayama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto, Tokyo, Peking, and CASS, studying under Xianlin Ji. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1995–2012) and headed Chuo Buddhist College (2022).

Sakurabe was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees, including a PhD, at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi. He served as a professor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1959) and Otani University (1971–1986).

Tanabe was a philosopher who studied at Tokyo and Kyoto, and in Germany under Heidegger, Rickert, and Husserl. A disciple of Kitaro Nishida, whom he succeeded in 1926, he served as an assistant professor at Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku was an early-modern Buddhist studies figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711).

Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, and in Europe under Richard von Garbe. He taught at Tohoku and Tokyo universities, and served as president of Komazawa University (1941).
Yasutani was a Buddhist studies and philosophy figure. He trained under several teachers, including Bokusan Nishiari and Sogaku Harada (1925–1943), and founded the Sanbo Zen organization in 1954.
Hadano was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Tohoku University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1953–1959) and later becoming professor emeritus.
Marlewicz is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Tadeusz Pobożniak. She holds a post as a professor at Jagiellonian University.
Safarewiczowa was a linguist who studied at Vilnius University (~1924–1928). She subsequently held a post at Jagiellonian University (~1945–1974).

O'Neal is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler (attested 2011) and serves as a co-director at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Kuløy worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as an officer for UNICEF (1972–1978, 1980–1984), edited the journal Kailash (~1973–1985), and founded Orchid Press and Bibliotheca Himalayica in 1982.

Saddhatissa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Vidyodaya Pirivena, Banaras Hindu University, and Edinburgh (PhD 1963). He led the London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990) and served as vice president of the Pali Text Society (1984–1990).
